kept.title: Insecure Header Forwarding on Cross-Domain Redirect
kept.description: Sensitive headers like Authorization and Cookie are only stripped if the protocol changes or the domain is not a superdomain. This allows leaking credentials to untrusted third-party domains if they share a suffix.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Attacker controls a malicious site at bad.example.com.
2. Victim site requests a resource on trusted.example.com sending sensitive Cookies.
3. Attacker triggers a 302 redirect to bad.example.com.
4. The package continues to send the session Cookie to the attacker's domain.
kept.impact: Session hijacking and unauthorized access to user data.

kept.title: Method Downgrade during Redirect
kept.description: The logic automatically converts POST/PUT requests to GET when encountering 301/302 redirects, which violates security expectations for non-idempotent operations and can lead to unexpected state changes on the redirected server.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Initiate a POST request with a sensitive body payload.
2. Receive a 301 redirect response.
3. The request is automatically retried as a GET request, potentially exposing sensitive parameters via URL logging or unintended state transitions.
kept.impact: Security bypass and potential data leakage via URL parameters.

kept.title: Lack of Strict Domain/Protocol Validation for Redirects
kept.description: The library allows redirection to any host and protocol provided by the Location header without sufficient white-listing, enabling potential SSRF attacks.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Direct the library to a server under attacker control.
2. The server responds with a 302 redirect to an internal service (e.g., http://localhost:6379).
3. The library follows the redirect to the internal service.
kept.impact: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) against internal infrastructure.

kept.title: Incomplete Sensitive Header Filtering
kept.description: The sensitiveHeaders list is static and hardcoded. Custom headers added by the application might not be included in the filtering logic, leading to accidental credential leakage.
steps_to_exploit: 1. User uses a custom header (e.g., X-API-KEY) for authentication.
2. This header is not in the hardcoded list.
3. The library forwards this header across domains during a redirect.
kept.impact: Leakage of custom authentication credentials to malicious third-party servers.

kept.title: Unbounded Memory Usage via Request Buffers
kept.description: The library buffers the entire request body to allow re-sending it upon redirection. While maxBodyLength exists, there is no limit on the number of concurrent requests, potentially leading to OOM attacks.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Flood the system with many concurrent requests containing large bodies.
2. Force the server to buffer all these bodies in memory for potential redirects.
3. The process runs out of memory.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Time-of-Check Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) in Header Removal
kept.description: Headers are removed/modified before sanitization occurs, and custom logic is applied after potential headers are already set, creating a mismatch in final request state.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Trigger a complex redirect scenario.
2. Intercept and manipulate the request state between the initial header filtering and the actual transmission.
kept.impact: Security policy bypass by ensuring sensitive headers are re-injected.

kept.title: Regex Injection via sensitiveHeaders
kept.description: The sensitiveHeaders list is converted into a RegExp object using join('|'). While escapeRegex is used, complex or unexpected character inputs could theoretically cause issues in older JS engines.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Supply a malicious header string in options.sensitiveHeaders.
2. Hope that the regex compilation logic fails or behaves unexpectedly to bypass filtering.
kept.impact: Bypassing security filters to leak sensitive headers.

kept.title: Missing SSL/TLS Certificate Validation Enforcement
kept.description: The package delegates request creation to the native http/https modules but does not explicitly enforce or check strict SSL/TLS configuration (e.g., rejectUnauthorized) for redirects.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Point the client to a URL with an invalid certificate.
2. The library follows the redirect to an attacker-controlled endpoint with an invalid SSL certificate without aborting.

kept.title: Inconsistent Redirect Loop Detection
kept.description: Loop detection is based on the count of redirects rather than an actual URL history check, which might not prevent all types of infinite loops or circular logical chains.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Create a chain of redirects that doesn't repeat the URL but is infinitely long.
2. The logic might not detect the cycle correctly until the limit is reached.
kept.impact: Potential Denial of Service by exhausting resources or time.

kept.title: Unsafe Handling of Redirected URLs
kept.description: Redirected URLs are parsed and passed back into the node request object without deep re-validation of host/port safety, potentially allowing protocol smuggling.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Server provides a location header like 'http://[::1]:80/'.
2. The library parses and blindly accepts the address for the next request.

kept.title: Information Disclosure via Debugging Logs
kept.description: The library uses a generic `debug` module which, if enabled in production, will log potentially sensitive URL information and header states to stdout.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Set DEBUG=follow-redirects* in the process environment.
2. Observe sensitive URLs and redirection logic in logs.
kept.impact: Leakage of internal architecture and user session info.

kept.title: Protocols exposure via inheritance
kept.description: The `wrap` function creates a new object prototype-linked to the original protocol, potentially inheriting unexpected methods or properties that could be exploited.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Enumerate prototype properties of the wrapped protocol.
2. Use those properties to manipulate request execution flow.
kept.impact: Unexpected behavior or security bypass in library usage.

kept.title: Weak Input Validation for URL Strings
kept.description: The validation for strings is relatively loose, relying on basic URL parsing which differs across node versions (useNativeURL switch).
steps_to_exploit: 1. Provide a malformed URL string that is interpreted differently by the legacy parser and the native URL parser.
kept.impact: Unexpected request routing or security filter evasion.

kept.title: Lack of Explicit Socket Cleanup
kept.description: While there is a timeout implementation, edge cases involving partial socket responses during a redirect might leave sockets hanging or not properly destroyed.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Trigger a fast redirect.
2. Race condition between socket destruction and new request setup.

kept.title: Use of unsafe `Object.assign` for Headers
kept.description: Headers are merged using `Object.assign` which can lead to prototype pollution if input options are improperly validated before passing.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Inject a malicious header property into the headers object that overrides prototype methods.
2. The library merges these into the request.
kept.impact: Denial of service or potential remote code execution via prototype manipulation.

proposed.title: Insecure Header Forwarding on Cross-Domain Redirect
Lack of Strict Domain/Protocol Validation for Redirects
Unbounded Memory Usage via Request Buffers
Weak Input Validation for URL Strings
